name_note: Haemophilus influenzae_I is one of several GTDB species split from Haemophilus influenzae, and the genomes placed here carry the NCBI name Haemophilus influenzae.

sentences.text: Nontypeable Haemophilus influenzae is described as a common colonizer of the human upper respiratory tract and a major pathogen in pediatric respiratory tract infections.
A review describes H. influenzae as a key model organism for mucosal pathobionts, associated with both asymptomatic colonization and a variety of disease states.
A systematic review and meta-analysis of 22 studies pooled carriage at 24.3 percent before Hib vaccination and 21.8 percent afterwards, with Hib carriage declining to 0.67 percent.
